concepts.def: The metals in the central block of the periodic table, between Group 2 and Group 3. They have properties that are similar to one another and different from the properties of the Group 1 metals.

The metals in the first column of the periodic table, such as lithium, sodium and potassium. They are soft, have low melting points and low densities, and react quickly with water, with oxygen and with the halogens.

Transition elements have much higher melting points than Group 1 metals. Chromium melts at about 1907 degrees C and iron at about 1538 degrees C, while sodium melts at about 98 degrees C and potassium at about 63 degrees C.

Transition elements are much denser than Group 1 metals. Copper is about 8.9 g/cm3 and nickel about 8.9 g/cm3, while sodium is about 0.97 g/cm3, which is less than the density of water, so sodium floats.

Transition elements such as chromium, iron, cobalt and nickel are hard and strong, which is why they are used for tools, machinery and hard-wearing chrome plating. Group 1 metals are soft enough to be cut with a knife.

Group 1 metals react with cold water, fizzing as hydrogen is released. Transition elements react very slowly or not at all with cold water, which is why copper is used for water pipes and why iron only rusts slowly in damp air.

A freshly cut Group 1 metal loses its shine within seconds as it reacts with oxygen in the air. Transition elements react far more slowly: copper stays shiny for months, and only turns black when it is heated strongly in air.

Group 1 metals react vigorously with the halogens. Transition elements react much less readily and usually need heating: hot iron reacts with chlorine to form iron(III) chloride, 2Fe + 3Cl2 gives 2FeCl3.
Many transition elements form more than one ion. Iron forms Fe2+ and Fe3+, copper forms Cu+ and Cu2+, and chromium forms Cr2+ and Cr3+, whereas a Group 1 metal only ever forms a 1+ ion.

Compounds of transition elements are usually coloured: copper(II) sulfate is blue, iron(II) sulfate is pale green, iron(III) oxide is red-brown, nickel(II) compounds are green and potassium manganate(VII) is purple. Group 1 compounds are usually white and give colourless solutions.

A substance that speeds up a reaction without being used up in the reaction. Many transition elements and their compounds are catalysts: iron in the Haber process, nickel for hardening vegetable oils, and manganese(IV) oxide for the decomposition of hydrogen peroxide.

The Roman numeral in a name such as iron(II) chloride or manganese(IV) oxide gives the charge on the metal ion, not the number of atoms in the formula. Iron(II) chloride is FeCl2 and iron(III) chloride is FeCl3.

mcqs.q: Which statement best describes the transition elements when they are compared with the Group 1 metals?
options: They react with water and with oxygen far more violently than Group 1 metals
They have properties that are similar to each other but different from Group 1 metals
They form only one fixed ion each, just like the Group 1 metals do
They have the same properties as Group 1 metals but higher atomic numbers
mcqs.explain: The specification states that the transition elements are metals with similar properties which are different from those of the elements in Group 1.

mcqs.q: Sodium melts at 98 degrees C and chromium melts at 1907 degrees C. Which conclusion do these values support?
options: The sodium sample was impure, because every metal melts well above 1000 degrees C
Chromium melts higher because it is the more reactive metal of the two
Melting point depends only on mass, so a heavier atom melts higher
Transition elements usually melt at much higher temperatures than Group 1 metals
mcqs.explain: This is the melting point difference the specification asks students to describe, and chromium against sodium is a clear example of it.

mcqs.q: A small piece of sodium floats on water, but a small piece of copper sinks. What does this show?
options: Sodium is less dense than water, while copper is far denser than water
Sodium cannot be a true metal, because every metal is denser than water is
Sodium melts at a low temperature, so a metal that melts easily is light
Copper sinks because it is the harder and stronger of these metals
mcqs.explain: Sodium is about 0.97 g/cm3 and copper about 8.9 g/cm3, which is the density difference between Group 1 and the transition elements.

mcqs.q: Potassium and nickel are each added to a separate beaker of cold water. What would you see?
options: Both metals fizz gently, but the nickel fizzes much more slowly
Neither metal reacts, because unreactive metals like nickel show no change
Potassium fizzes and melts; the nickel does not change
The nickel fizzes strongly while the potassium slowly darkens
mcqs.explain: Potassium reacts vigorously with cold water, releasing hydrogen and melting from the heat given out, while nickel shows no visible reaction.

mcqs.q: Freshly cut sodium and freshly polished copper are both left out in air. What happens to their shiny surfaces?
options: The copper stays shiny for ever, because it never reacts with oxygen
The sodium stays shiny, while the copper dulls in a few seconds
Both dull at the same rate, since both of them react with oxygen
The sodium dulls within seconds; the copper only dulls slowly over months
mcqs.explain: A cut surface of sodium is coated with oxide almost at once, whereas copper reacts with oxygen very slowly unless it is heated strongly.

mcqs.q: Sodium and iron are each heated in chlorine gas. Which statement about these two reactions is correct?
options: Sodium reacts violently, while iron reacts less readily to give FeCl3
Iron reacts far more violently, because it is the harder, stronger metal
Only sodium reacts, as transition metals never react with halogens
Both react at the same rate, because chlorine is very reactive
mcqs.explain: Group 1 metals react vigorously with halogens; hot iron reacts less readily, forming iron(III) chloride, 2Fe + 3Cl2 gives 2FeCl3.

mcqs.q: Element X melts at 1495 degrees C, has a density of 8.9 g/cm3 and shows no reaction with cold water. Which element is X most likely to be?
options: Sodium, because metals such as sodium melt at above 1000 degrees C
Lithium, because all metals are dense and sink in water
Cobalt, because those values are typical of a transition metal
Calcium, because it reacts only slowly with the cold water in a beaker
mcqs.explain: Cobalt melts at 1495 degrees C and has a density of 8.9 g/cm3; a high melting point, high density and no reaction with cold water are the transition metal pattern.

mcqs.q: Which set of properties is typical of many of the transition elements?
options: One fixed ion charge, white compounds and use as catalysts
Ions of different charges, coloured compounds, catalysts
Ions of different charges, white compounds and low densities
One fixed ion charge, coloured compounds and low melting points
mcqs.explain: The specification states that many transition elements have ions with different charges, form coloured compounds and are useful as catalysts.

mcqs.q: Copper(II) sulfate solution is blue, but sodium sulfate solution is colourless. What is the best explanation?
options: Copper is a transition element, and its compounds are usually coloured
The sulfate ion gives the blue colour in any sulfate solution
Both compounds are colourless, so the blue must come from an impurity
The solution is blue because copper metal itself is blue
mcqs.explain: Forming coloured compounds is one of the properties the specification gives for transition elements, exemplified here by a compound of copper.

mcqs.q: Iron forms two chlorides, FeCl2 and FeCl3. What does the (II) in the name iron(II) chloride tell you?
options: Two chlorine atoms are joined to each of the iron atoms
The iron atom has lost two protons from the nucleus
It is the second of the chlorides that iron forms
The iron ion in this compound carries a charge of 2+
mcqs.explain: The Roman numeral gives the charge on the transition metal ion, which is what lets iron form both iron(II) and iron(III) compounds.

mcqs.q: Hydrogen peroxide decomposes slowly. When manganese(IV) oxide is added, oxygen is given off quickly. What is the manganese(IV) oxide doing?
options: It is used up in the reaction, so more must be added each time
It speeds up the reaction and is not itself used up
It raises the total volume of oxygen that can be given off
It reacts with the peroxide to release the oxygen
mcqs.explain: Manganese(IV) oxide is a catalyst, one of the uses of transition metal compounds that the specification names.

mcqs.q: Sodium can be cut with a knife, but chromium is used for tools and hard-wearing plating. What does this show?
options: Chromium is harder, so it is also the more reactive of the two
Transition elements are hard and strong, while Group 1 metals are soft
Sodium is too soft to be counted as a proper metal at all
Hardness, density and melting point are really one single property
mcqs.explain: This is the strength and hardness difference the specification asks students to describe, shown here by chromium against sodium.
